description: Grey granite plates held by unbroken salmon-pink seams. In armour a crushing blow arrives as a shove, a fall as a bruise.
lore: Pick one up expecting a pebble and you get something else, because it is not one piece. The body is grey granite in plates, and every plate is held to the next by a seam of salmon pink, so the thing holds the way a wall holds rather than the way a stone does, which is to say by how it is joined. That is also exactly how it is graded. Seams unbroken and running right round the body is a full one. Pink that is dashed, or pinched out, or stops and starts again a finger further on, is a poor one, and a poor one comes apart in service, and everyone in the trade knows somebody it came apart on.

It is the one stone on the bench a good cutter is glad to break. Struck along a seam it opens into two clean plates and both of them still work, which is true of nothing else on the shelf. Struck across the grain it goes to gravel and is worth nothing to anyone. So the pink has to be read before the hammer comes down, and the people who can read it do very little else for a living. What comes off that bench and into armour does not make the armour lighter; it makes the ground feel closer. Drops come off short. Whatever lands on the wearer still lands, and simply arrives without the part of it that was going to break something.

There is a rule in the trade that gets repeated without much enjoyment, which is that the best armour does not come off fighters. Stones out of things that struck, and struck hard, go into blades, which is where they are wanted and where they do good service. The stones that will actually keep a person in one piece come off animals that never struck anything in their existence and spent the whole of it with one question in front of them, which is where to be standing when something heavy happens. What is pressed into one of these is not courage and it is not strength. It is somewhere to be. Anyone who has stood under a roof they were not sure about, in the dark, listening to it, has held that same thought for a minute or two. This one held it for a lifetime and held it until it went to granite.
